core_obligations: Starting from inverse dominant rational maps f : U -> Y and g : V -> X, shrink U so that f factors through V and U -> V -> X is the inclusion (proof lines 9897-9904).
By symmetry produce an open subspace V' of V over which g factors through U with V' -> U -> Y the identity (proof lines 9905-9907).
Realize the preimage of |V'| under |U| -> |V| as the underlying set of an open subspace U' of U, so that U' -> V factors through V' and V' -> U factors through U' (proof lines 9908-9912).
Conclude that U' -> V' and V' -> U' are mutually inverse isomorphisms of algebraic spaces over S (proof lines 9913-9916).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for algebraic spaces X and Y over S with irreducible underlying topological spaces, X and Y are birational if and only if they contain nonempty open subspaces U and V isomorphic over S (source lines 9888-9895). One direction is the definition; the other is a reduction that shrinks the two opens step by step: from inverse dominant rational maps f : U -> Y and g : V -> X one arranges that f factors through V and that U -> V -> X is the inclusion, then symmetrically produces V' contained in V over which g factors through U with V' -> U -> Y the identity, and finally takes U' to be the open subspace of U whose underlying set is the preimage of |V'|, so that the two morphisms become mutually inverse.
